# DECISIONS — Live Work Surface session data plane

## What I looked at
Traced the flush path end to end: `LiveWorkSurface.tsx` → `POST /api/devcase/session/[id]`
(`app/api/devcase/session/[id]/route.ts`) → `saveDevSessionFiles` / `appendDevSessionEvents`
(`app/_lib/db/devcase.ts`). The brief also names a chat channel
(`app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts`, `pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py`) — neither
exists in this repo snapshot. I did not invent a chat surface to "fix"; noted below as scope.

## The one thing I fixed
Every 8s (`FLUSH_MS`), the client POSTed `{ events, files }` where `files` was the FULL seed
tree (every file, full contents) regardless of whether anything changed. `saveDevSessionFiles`
does an unconditional `UPDATE ... SET files_json = ?` with that whole blob. Most 8s ticks are a
candidate reading/thinking, not typing — so the common case is: re-serialize and re-write the
entire file tree for no reason, on a timer, for every active session.

Fix: track a `filesDirtyRef` flag, set on edit, cleared after a flush that included files lands.
`flush()` now only sends `files` when dirty or on submit (final state always persisted). If a
tick has neither pending events nor dirty files, it skips the network call entirely.

**Rejected alternative:** debounce/diff the file contents server-side (send only changed files,
byte-diff, etc.). More correct in theory, touches the server contract and DB shape, more surface
to get wrong in a timebox. A boolean dirty flag on the client gets ~the same win (skip idle
writes, which is the dominant case) for a five-line change in one file.

**Rejected alternative:** lower `FLUSH_MS` concerns / event batching — events are already
capped and debounced (`MAX_EVENTS`, `EDIT_DEBOUNCE_MS`); I read enough to see that path wasn't
the redundant one and left it alone.

## Verification (manual, no test run per scope)
- Read the new `flush()` logic through by hand for both branches: dirty-with-batch,
  dirty-without-batch, clean-with-batch, clean-without-batch (early return, no fetch).
- Failure path: on a rejected/erroring flush, `filesDirtyRef` is only cleared inside the
  success branch (after `r.ok`), so a failed send correctly retries files on the next tick
  instead of silently dropping them. Events already had this re-buffer behavior; unchanged.
- Server side needs no change: `Array.isArray(body.files)` on the route already treats an
  absent `files` key as "nothing to save" — an events-only heartbeat is not new server surface,
  it's the existing optional-key path.
- Did not run the dev server or the test suite (out of scope for this pass); this is a light
  manual read-through, not an executed check.

## MID-FLIGHT: 10x concurrent candidates next month
Read as: (1) whatever ships must not fall over at 10x flush/chat volume, (2) "context bloat we
absorb today becomes real money" — i.e. someone is worried about LLM spend on the chat side
specifically.

**My call: the flush fix already is the 10x accommodation, and I'm doing nothing further.**
At idle-dominant traffic (which is most of a candidate's session — reading a brief, thinking),
the dirty-check turns most flush ticks into either a no-op or an events-only heartbeat instead
of a full file-tree rewrite. That's not a new mitigation for scale, it's the same fix — it just
matters more at 10x because the redundant work scales linearly with concurrent idle sessions,
and this removes the majority of it without touching the request shape, the DB schema, or
adding any new capacity-planning surface (no rate limiter, no queue, no backpressure — none of
that was asked for by evidence, and I didn't have time to size it correctly anyway).

**What I'm explicitly declaring out of scope, in writing:** the chat/model-context cost concern.
There is no chat endpoint or model call in this repo snapshot (`app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/`
and `pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py` don't exist) — I'm not going to fabricate a fix for code
that isn't here. If a chat surface lands later, the first thing I'd check before 10x ships is
whether it resends full conversation history as context on every turn (the same "resend
everything, every tick" shape as the bug I just fixed) — that's exactly the kind of thing that's
cheap today and expensive at 10x. Flagging it as the next thing to look at, not fixing it blind.

## Explicitly not done (honesty pass)
- No test run, no dev server boot, no lint/typecheck — manual read-through only, as scoped.
- No server-side diffing/patching of the file tree — client-side dirty flag only.
- No look at chat.py / chat route — doesn't exist in this snapshot; see mid-flight note above.
- No rate limiting or backpressure work for the 10x claim — reasoned about, not built.

chat.text: Client is app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx, flush route is app/api/devcase/session/[id]/route.ts. Does the flush body always include the full `files` array on every 8s tick, even when nothing changed?

Yes — flush() always sends `files: filesRef.current` (the whole seed tree, full contents) on every interval tick, and saveDevSessionFiles does an unconditional UPDATE files_json = ? on every call, regardless of whether any file changed since the last flush.
Cheapest fix to stop that idle-tick full-tree resend without touching the server route or DB shape — client-side only, minimal diff?

Add a dirty ref set on edit and cleared after a flush that included files succeeds; only put `files` in the POST body when dirty or on submit. If a tick has no pending events and no dirty files, skip the fetch entirely.
Does app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts or pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py actually exist in this repo, or am I chasing a brief that describes a surface that isn't here?

Neither path exists in this checkout — there is no chat route under app/api/devcase/session/[id]/ and no chat.py under pipeline/jobfit/devcase/. The only real session data-plane surface here is the flush endpoint.

notes: Flush was resending the full file tree every 8s even when idle; gated it behind a dirty flag. Chat/model-context path named in the brief does not exist in this repo, so I left it alone and said so rather than fabricate a fix.
